records.source: וַיְהִ֣י׀בַּשָּׁנָ֣ה הַהִ֗יא בְּרֵאשִׁית֙ מַמְלֶ֨כֶת֙ צִדְקִיָּ֣ה מֶֽלֶךְ־יְהוּדָ֔ה בַּשָּׁנָה֙ הָֽרְבִעִ֔ית בַּחֹ֖דֶשׁ הַחֲמִישִׁ֑י אָמַ֣ר אֵלַ֡י חֲנַנְיָה֩ בֶן־עַזּ֨וּר הַנָּבִ֜יא אֲשֶׁ֤ר מִגִּבְעוֹן֙ בְּבֵ֣ית יְהוָ֔ה לְעֵינֵ֧י הַכֹּהֲנִ֛ים וְכָל־הָעָ֖ם לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And it was in the year the that, in [the] beginning of [the] reign of Zedekiah king of Judah, in the year the fourth, in the month the fifth, said to me Hananiah son of Azzur the prophet who [was] from Gibeon in [the] house of Yahweh before [the] eyes of the priests and all the people, saying,
pieces: In that same year, early in the reign of Zedekiah king of Judah, in the fifth month of the fourth year, the prophet Hananiah son of Azzur, from Gibeon, spoke to me. It was in the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, with the priests and all the people looking on:

L.1: And it was in that year, at [the] beginning of the reign of Zedekiah king of Judah, in the fourth year, in the fifth month, [that] Hananiah son of Azzur, the prophet who [was] from Gibeon, said to me in the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, before the eyes of the priests and all the people, saying,

R.1: That same year, early in the time when Zedekiah was king of Judah, Hananiah son of Azzur spoke to me. It was the fifth month of Zedekiah's fourth year as king. Hananiah was a prophet from the town of Gibeon. He spoke to me in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple, while the priests and all the people were watching. He said:

decisions.choice: in that same year: the year of chapter 27, when Jeremiah wore a yoke as a sign
decisions.reason: The story follows straight on from 27:1-22. Jeremiah had put on straps and bars of a yoke at the LORD's command (27:2) and told Zedekiah and the nations to serve the king of Babylon (27:12). Hananiah answers that message here.

decisions.choice: "at the beginning of the reign" and "in the fourth year" stand side by side: the fourth year counts as the early part of an eleven-year reign
alternatives: two different dates joined together, the second correcting the first
decisions.reason: Zedekiah reigned eleven years (2 Kings 24:18), so his fourth year can still be called the first part of his reign. The written consonants at "in the year" read "in the year of"; the reading tradition has "in the year", with no difference in sense. The Greek translation does not have "in that year, at the beginning of the reign" and simply dates the event to the fourth year of Zedekiah.

decisions.choice: to me: the account begins in Jeremiah's own voice and from verse 5 on speaks of him by name
decisions.reason: Chapter 27 is told in the first person (27:2, 12, 16), and this verse carries that on. From verse 5 the narrator refers to "Jeremiah the prophet".

decisions.choice: Hananiah, the prophet from Gibeon: a recognized prophet, given the same title as Jeremiah
decisions.reason: Gibeon was a town of Benjamin a few miles north-west of Jerusalem, and one of the priests' towns (Joshua 21:17). The narrator calls Hananiah "the prophet" just as he calls Jeremiah; the story itself shows which of them the LORD sent (verse 15).

decisions.choice: the town of Gibeon; temple; were watching
decisions.reason: Readable splits the long date into short sentences, says that Gibeon is a town, calls the house of the LORD the temple, and explains "before the eyes of" as watching.

records.heading: Hananiah breaks the yoke

records.source: כֹּֽה־אָמַ֞ר יְהוָ֧ה צְבָא֛וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֵאמֹ֑ר שָׁבַ֞רְתִּי אֶת־עֹ֖ל מֶ֥לֶךְ בָּבֶֽל׃
records.gloss: Thus says Yahweh of hosts, [the] God of Israel, saying, I have broken the yoke of [the] king of Babylon.
pieces: "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, the God of Israel, says this: I have broken the yoke of the king of Babylon.

L.2: "Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts, the God of Israel, saying: I have broken the yoke of the king of Babylon.

R.2: "This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, the God of Israel, says: I have broken the king of Babylon's yoke, the one he put on the nations.

decisions.choice: I have broken: spoken as already done, though it is to happen within two years (verses 3, 11)
decisions.reason: The verb is a completed form used for something so sure that it can be spoken of as finished. Verse 4 says the same thing as a future: "I will break the yoke".

decisions.choice: the yoke: the rule of Babylon over Judah and the nations, the picture of Jeremiah's sign in chapter 27
decisions.reason: Jeremiah wore a yoke to show that the nations must bend their necks under the king of Babylon (27:2, 8, 11-12). Hananiah takes up the same picture and turns it around.

decisions.choice: Hananiah speaks with the full formula Jeremiah uses
decisions.reason: "Thus says the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel" is the opening Jeremiah used for the opposite message (27:4, 19, 21). Both prophets claim the same authority, which is why the test of verse 9 is needed.

decisions.choice: that the king of Babylon put on the nations
decisions.reason: Readable says whose necks the yoke is on, from 27:8 and verse 11.

records.source: בְּע֣וֹד׀שְׁנָתַ֣יִם יָמִ֗ים אֲנִ֤י מֵשִׁיב֙ אֶל־הַמָּק֣וֹם הַזֶּ֔ה אֶֽת־כָּל־כְּלֵ֖י בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר לָקַ֜ח נְבוּכַדנֶאצַּ֤רמֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶל֙ מִן־הַמָּק֣וֹם הַזֶּ֔ה וַיְבִיאֵ֖ם בָּבֶֽל׃
records.gloss: Within yet two years of days I [am] bringing back to the place the this all [the] vessels of [the] house of Yahweh that took Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon from the place the this and he brought them [to] Babylon.
pieces: Within two full years I will bring back to this place all the vessels of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon took from here and carried to Babylon.

L.3: Within two years [of] days I [am] bringing back to this place all the vessels of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon took from this place and brought to Babylon.

R.3: Before two years are over, I will bring back to this place all the valuable objects from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon took away to Babylon.

decisions.choice: two years of days: two full years, a short and fixed time
decisions.reason: Adding "days" to a span of time marks it as complete (Genesis 41:1). The short time contrasts with what Jeremiah said: the vessels would stay in Babylon until the LORD acted (27:22), and the exile would last seventy years (25:11; 29:10).

decisions.choice: the vessels of the house of the LORD: the gold and bronze bowls, basins and other temple objects taken in 597 BC
decisions.reason: Nebuchadnezzar took them when he carried King Jehoiachin into exile (2 Kings 24:13). Other prophets had already promised they would soon come back, and Jeremiah had called that promise a lie (27:16).

decisions.choice: Nebuchadnezzar: the same king who is often called Nebuchadrezzar in Jeremiah
decisions.reason: Jeremiah has two spellings of the Babylonian king's name. Chapters 27-29 use the form with n (27:6); each verse keeps the form its Hebrew has.

decisions.choice: valuable objects
decisions.reason: Readable says what the vessels were rather than using the older word "vessels".

records.source: וְאֶת־יְכָנְיָ֣ה בֶן־יְהוֹיָקִ֣ים מֶֽלֶךְ־יְ֠הוּדָה וְאֶת־כָּל־גָּל֨וּת יְהוּדָ֜ה הַבָּאִ֣ים בָּבֶ֗לָה אֲנִ֥י מֵשִׁ֛יב אֶל־הַמָּק֥וֹם הַזֶּ֖ה נְאֻם־יְהוָ֑ה כִּ֣י אֶשְׁבֹּ֔ר אֶת־עֹ֖ל מֶ֥לֶךְ בָּבֶֽל׃
records.gloss: And Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim king of Judah and all [the] exile[s] of Judah the coming [to] Babylon I [am] bringing back to the place the this, declares Yahweh, for I will break [the] yoke of [the] king of Babylon.
pieces: I will also bring Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim king of Judah back to this place, with every exile of Judah who went off to Babylon, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; for I will break the king of Babylon's yoke."

L.4: And Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim king of Judah and all the exiles of Judah who went to Babylon I [am] bringing back to this place, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, for I will break the yoke of the king of Babylon."

R.4: I will also bring back Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim, the king of Judah, and all the people of Judah who were taken away to Babylon. I will bring them back to this place, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, because I am going to break the king of Babylon's yoke."

decisions.choice: Jeconiah: the king also called Jehoiachin and Coniah
decisions.reason: He reigned three months and was taken to Babylon in 597 BC (2 Kings 24:8-15). Jeremiah calls him Coniah in 22:24, 28 and Jeconiah in 24:1 and 27:20; this verse uses Jeconiah.

decisions.choice: Hananiah's promise contradicts what the LORD had said through Jeremiah
decisions.reason: Jeremiah had said that Coniah would never come back to the land (22:24-27) and that the exiles should settle in Babylon (24:5-7; 29:4-10). The two promises cannot both be from the LORD.

decisions.choice: the exiles: the people taken into exile with the king
decisions.reason: The word names the whole deported community, the officials, craftsmen and others (24:1; 29:1-2).

decisions.choice: who were taken away
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says they "went" to Babylon; Readable makes clear they did not go by choice (2 Kings 24:14-16).

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ יִרְמְיָ֣ה הַנָּבִ֔יא אֶל־חֲנַנְיָ֖ה הַנָּבִ֑יא לְעֵינֵ֤י הַכֹּֽהֲנִים֙ וּלְעֵינֵ֣י כָל־הָעָ֔ם הָעֹמְדִ֖ים בְּבֵ֥ית יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And said Jeremiah the prophet to Hananiah the prophet before [the] eyes of the priests and before [the] eyes of all the people the standing in [the] house of Yahweh,
pieces: Then the prophet Jeremiah spoke to the prophet Hananiah in the presence of the priests and of all the people standing there in the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.5: And Jeremiah the prophet said to Hananiah the prophet, before the eyes of the priests and before the eyes of all the people who were standing in the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}},

R.5: Then the prophet Jeremiah answered the prophet Hananiah. The priests and all the people standing in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple were listening.

decisions.choice: Jeremiah the prophet ... Hananiah the prophet: two men with the same title, face to face
decisions.reason: The narrator gives both men the same title side by side. Which of them truly speaks for the LORD is the question the chapter answers.

decisions.choice: before the eyes of: in full view, publicly
decisions.reason: As in verse 1, the answer is given before the same priests and people who heard Hananiah's claim.

decisions.choice: were listening
decisions.reason: Readable puts the witnesses in a sentence of their own and says what they were doing.

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ יִרְמְיָ֣ה הַנָּבִ֔יא אָמֵ֕ן כֵּ֖ן יַעֲשֶׂ֣ה יְהוָ֑ה יָקֵ֤ם יְהוָה֙ אֶת־דְּבָרֶ֔יךָ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נִבֵּ֗אתָ לְהָשִׁ֞יב כְּלֵ֤י בֵית־יְהוָה֙ וְכָל־הַגּוֹלָ֔ה מִבָּבֶ֖ל אֶל־הַמָּק֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃
records.gloss: And said Jeremiah the prophet, Amen, so may do Yahweh; may establish Yahweh your words that you have prophesied, to bring back [the] vessels of [the] house of Yahweh and all the exile[s] from Babylon to the place the this.
pieces: The prophet Jeremiah said, "Amen! May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} do just that! May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} make the words you have prophesied come true, and bring the vessels of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and all the exiles back from Babylon to this place.

L.6: And Jeremiah the prophet said, "Amen! So may {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} do! May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} establish your words that you have prophesied, to bring back the vessels of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and all the exiles from Babylon to this place.

R.6: Jeremiah said, "Amen! I hope {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} does this! I hope {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} makes your message come true. I hope {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brings the valuable objects from the temple and all the captives back from Babylon to this place.

decisions.choice: Amen: "so be it", agreeing with a wish
decisions.reason: Jeremiah agrees with what Hananiah hopes for, not with his claim to speak for the LORD; the "but" of verse 7 shows the difference.

decisions.choice: establish: make a word stand, carry it out
decisions.reason: The verb means to make something stand up. Said of a word, it means to fulfil it (1 Samuel 1:23).

decisions.choice: Jeremiah wishes good for his people even while he announces judgment
decisions.reason: He had prayed for them and taken no pleasure in the day of disaster (17:16; 18:20). His "Amen" is honest, but it does not change what the LORD has said.

decisions.choice: I hope
decisions.reason: The verbs are wishes ("may he do"). Readable puts the wish in everyday words.

records.source: אַךְ־שְׁמַֽע־נָא֙ הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר אָנֹכִ֖י דֹּבֵ֣ר בְּאָזְנֶ֑יךָ וּבְאָזְנֵ֖י כָּל־הָעָֽם׃
records.gloss: But hear please the word the this which I [am] speaking in your ears and in [the] ears of all the people.
pieces: But listen now to this word that I speak in your hearing and in the hearing of all the people.

L.7: But hear now this word that I [am] speaking in your ears and in the ears of all the people.

R.7: But listen to what I am going to say to you and to all these people.

decisions.choice: but: a strong turn from the wish to a warning
decisions.reason: The small word means "only" or "however" and limits what was just said: the wish of verse 6 is not a prophecy.

decisions.choice: in your ears: so that you and everyone hear it
decisions.reason: Speaking "in the ears" of someone means speaking openly to them; the people are witnesses again (verse 5).

decisions.choice: in your hearing
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the idea of hearing in a familiar English phrase; Literal keeps "ears".

records.source: הַנְּבִיאִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר הָי֧וּ לְפָנַ֛י וּלְפָנֶ֖יךָ מִן־הָֽעוֹלָ֑ם וַיִּנָּ֨בְא֜וּ אֶל־אֲרָצ֤וֹת רַבּוֹת֙ וְעַל־מַמְלָכ֣וֹת גְּדֹל֔וֹת לְמִלְחָמָ֖ה וּלְרָעָ֥ה וּלְדָֽבֶר׃
records.gloss: The prophets who were before me and before you from antiquity, and they prophesied against lands many and against kingdoms great, of war and of disaster and of pestilence.
pieces: The prophets who came before you and me, from ancient times, prophesied war, disaster and plague against many countries and great kingdoms.

L.8: The prophets who were before me and before you from of old prophesied against many lands and against great kingdoms, of war and of disaster and of pestilence.

R.8: There were prophets long before you and me. They spoke against many countries and great kingdoms, warning them of war, disaster and disease.

decisions.choice: disaster
decisions.reason: The standard Hebrew text reads "disaster". Some Hebrew manuscripts read "famine", a word that differs by one letter and would give the triad "sword, famine and pestilence" found often in Jeremiah (14:12; 21:7). The sense of the verse is the same either way.

decisions.choice: prophets of judgment stand in a long line; a warning of disaster fits what true prophets have always said
decisions.reason: Jeremiah points to earlier prophets who spoke against nations (compare Micah, quoted in 26:18). A message like his needs no special proof; a message of peace does (verse 9).

decisions.choice: against: messages of judgment directed at nations
decisions.reason: The words can also mean "concerning", but the list that follows (war, disaster, pestilence) shows they were warnings.

decisions.choice: plague (Balanced); disease (Readable)
decisions.reason: The word for pestilence follows the book's wording: "pestilence" at Literal, "plague" at Balanced and "disease" at Readable.

records.source: הַנָּבִ֕יא אֲשֶׁ֥ר יִנָּבֵ֖א לְשָׁל֑וֹם בְּבֹא֙ דְּבַ֣ר הַנָּבִ֗יא יִוָּדַע֙ הַנָּבִ֔יא אֲשֶׁר־שְׁלָח֥וֹ יְהוָ֖ה בֶּאֱמֶֽת׃
records.gloss: The prophet who prophesies of peace, when comes [the] word of the prophet, will be known the prophet whom has sent him Yahweh in truth.
pieces: But the prophet who prophesies peace will be known as one whom {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has truly sent when his word comes to pass."

L.9: The prophet who prophesies of peace, when the word of the prophet comes [to pass], the prophet will be known whom {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has sent in truth."

R.9: But when a prophet says there will be peace, people will know that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} really sent him only when what he said actually happens."

decisions.choice: the test of Deuteronomy 18:21-22, applied to a promise of peace
decisions.reason: The law says that a word spoken in the LORD's name which does not happen was not spoken by the LORD (Deuteronomy 18:21-22). Jeremiah applies it to Hananiah: wait and see whether the two years bring peace.

decisions.choice: peace: safety and well-being, the end of the threat from Babylon
decisions.reason: Other prophets were promising "peace" when disaster was coming (6:14; 14:13; 23:17).

decisions.choice: in truth: truly, really sent
decisions.reason: The phrase goes with "sent": the question is whether the LORD actually sent the prophet.

decisions.choice: But; only (Readable)
decisions.reason: The contrast with verse 8 is implied by the order of the sentences. Balanced and Readable add "but", and Readable adds "only" to make the condition plain.

records.source: וַיִּקַּ֞ח חֲנַנְיָ֤ה הַנָּבִיא֙ אֶת־הַמּוֹטָ֔ה מֵעַ֕ל צַוַּ֖אר יִרְמְיָ֣ה הַנָּבִ֑יא וַֽיִּשְׁבְּרֵֽהוּ׃
records.gloss: And took Hananiah the prophet the yoke-bar from upon [the] neck of Jeremiah the prophet and he broke it.
pieces: Then the prophet Hananiah took the yoke bar off the neck of the prophet Jeremiah and broke it.

L.10: And Hananiah the prophet took the yoke bar from upon the neck of Jeremiah the prophet and broke it.

R.10: Then Hananiah took the wooden yoke bar off Jeremiah's neck and broke it.

decisions.choice: the yoke bar: the wooden crossbar of a yoke, tied on with straps
decisions.reason: Jeremiah had made straps and bars and put them on his neck as the LORD commanded (27:2). The bar lay across the neck of an animal pulling a load.

decisions.choice: breaking the bar: an acted sign against Jeremiah's sign
decisions.reason: Prophets acted out their messages (1 Kings 22:11). Hananiah breaks Jeremiah's sign to show his own message, as he explains in verse 11.

decisions.choice: the wooden yoke bar
decisions.reason: Readable says what the bar was made of (verse 13) and leaves out the repeated title "the prophet".

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר חֲנַנְיָה֩ לְעֵינֵ֨י כָל־הָעָ֜ם לֵאמֹ֗ר כֹּה֮ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָה֒ כָּ֣כָה אֶשְׁבֹּ֞ר אֶת־עֹ֣ל׀נְבֻֽכַדְנֶאצַּ֣ר מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶ֗ל בְּעוֹד֙ שְׁנָתַ֣יִם יָמִ֔ים מֵעַ֕לצַוַּ֖אר כָּל־הַגּוֹיִ֑ם וַיֵּ֛לֶךְ יִרְמְיָ֥ה הַנָּבִ֖יא לְדַרְכּֽוֹ׃פ
records.gloss: And said Hananiah before [the] eyes of all the people, saying, Thus says Yahweh, Thus I will break [the] yoke of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon within yet two years of days from upon [the] neck of all the nations. And went Jeremiah the prophet to his way.
pieces: And Hananiah spoke in the presence of all the people: "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this: In just this way, within two full years, I will break the yoke of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and take it off the neck of every nation." Then the prophet Jeremiah went away.

L.11: And Hananiah said before the eyes of all the people, saying, "Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: Thus I will break the yoke of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon within two years [of] days from upon the neck of all the nations." And Jeremiah the prophet went his way.

R.11: Hananiah said to all the people, "This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: In the same way, I will break the yoke of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon. Before two years are over, I will take it off the necks of all the nations." Then the prophet Jeremiah left.

decisions.choice: in this way: the broken bar explained as a sign of what God will do
decisions.reason: The word points to what Hananiah has just done: as the bar is broken, so Babylon's rule will be broken.

decisions.choice: all the nations: the peoples whose envoys had come to Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Chapter 27 names Edom, Moab, Ammon, Tyre and Sidon (27:3), all told to serve Babylon (27:6-8).

decisions.choice: Jeremiah went his way: he left without an answer
decisions.reason: He gives no reply until the LORD speaks to him (verse 12); he does not answer Hananiah's sign with words of his own.

decisions.choice: two sentences; left
decisions.reason: Readable splits the promise into two sentences and says simply that Jeremiah left.

records.source: וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר־יְהוָ֖ה אֶֽל־יִרְמְיָ֑ה אַ֠חֲרֵי שְׁב֞וֹר חֲנַנְיָ֤ה הַנָּבִיא֙ אֶת־הַמּוֹטָ֔ה מֵעַ֗ל צַוַּ֛אר יִרְמְיָ֥ה הַנָּבִ֖יא לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And came [the] word of Yahweh to Jeremiah after broke Hananiah the prophet the yoke-bar from upon [the] neck of Jeremiah the prophet, saying,
pieces: After the prophet Hananiah had broken the yoke bar off the neck of the prophet Jeremiah, the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to Jeremiah:

L.12: And the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to Jeremiah, after Hananiah the prophet had broken the yoke bar from upon the neck of Jeremiah the prophet, saying:

R.12: After Hananiah broke the wooden yoke bar that was on Jeremiah's neck, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave Jeremiah this message:

decisions.choice: after: the time is not given
decisions.reason: The word came once the bar had been broken; the text does not say how long Jeremiah waited.

decisions.choice: the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah (Balanced); the LORD gave Jeremiah this message (Readable)
decisions.reason: The formula follows the book's settled wording for "the word of the LORD came".

records.heading: A yoke of iron

records.source: הָלוֹךְ֩ וְאָמַרְתָּ֨ אֶל־חֲנַנְיָ֜ה לֵאמֹ֗ר כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה מוֹטֹ֥ת עֵ֖ץ שָׁבָ֑רְתָּ וְעָשִׂ֥יתָ תַחְתֵּיהֶ֖ן מֹט֥וֹת בַּרְזֶֽל׃
records.gloss: Go and you will say to Hananiah, saying, Thus says Yahweh, bars of wood you have broken, and you have made in place of them bars of iron.
pieces: "Go and tell Hananiah, '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this: You have broken bars of wood, but in their place you have made bars of iron.

L.13: "Go, and say to Hananiah, saying: 'Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: Bars of wood you have broken, and you have made in their place bars of iron.

R.13: "Go and tell Hananiah, 'This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: You broke the wooden bars of a yoke. But you have only made iron bars to take their place.

decisions.choice: you have made: by breaking the wooden yoke, Hananiah has brought on a harder one
decisions.reason: The Hebrew form can also look ahead ("you will make"). The Greek translation reads "I will make". Either way, resisting the LORD's sign does not remove the yoke; it makes it heavier.

decisions.choice: bars of iron: a yoke that cannot be broken
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 28:48 warns of "a yoke of iron" put on the neck of a people who will not serve the LORD. Verse 14 gives the meaning.

decisions.choice: but; only (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew joins the clauses with "and". Balanced and Readable bring out the contrast, and Readable adds "only" to show the result was the opposite of what Hananiah wanted.

records.source: כִּ֣י כֹֽה־אָמַר֩ יְהוָ֨ה צְבָא֜וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל עֹ֣ל בַּרְזֶ֡ל נָתַ֜תִּי עַל־צַוַּ֣אר׀כָּל־הַגּוֹיִ֣ם הָאֵ֗לֶּה לַעֲבֹ֛ד אֶת־נְבֻכַדְנֶאצַּ֥ר מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶ֖ל וַעֲבָדֻ֑הוּ וְגַ֛ם אֶת־חַיַּ֥ת הַשָּׂדֶ֖ה נָתַ֥תִּי לֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: For thus says Yahweh of hosts, [the] God of Israel, a yoke of iron I have put upon [the] neck of all the nations the these to serve Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and they will serve him; and also [the] animals of the field I have given to him.
pieces: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, the God of Israel, says this: It is a yoke of iron that I have put on the neck of all these nations, so that they serve Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon; and serve him they will. I have given him even the wild animals.'"

L.14: For thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts, the God of Israel: A yoke of iron I have put upon the neck of all these nations, to serve Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and they will serve him; and even the animals of the field I have given to him.'"

R.14: For this is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, the God of Israel, says: I have put an iron yoke on the necks of all these nations. They must serve Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and they will do it. I have even put the wild animals under his control.'"

decisions.choice: even the animals of the field: the words of 27:6 repeated
decisions.reason: In 27:6 the LORD said he had given all these lands to Nebuchadnezzar, and even the wild animals to serve him. The repetition shows that nothing in the earlier message has changed.

decisions.choice: it is the LORD who has put the yoke on the nations
decisions.reason: Hananiah said the LORD had broken Babylon's yoke (verse 2). Here the LORD says he himself put it there, and made it of iron.

decisions.choice: under his control
decisions.reason: Readable says in what sense the animals are "given" to the king.

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יִרְמְיָ֧ה הַנָּבִ֛יא אֶל־חֲנַנְיָ֥ה הַנָּבִ֖יא שְׁמַֽע־נָ֣א חֲנַנְיָ֑ה לֹֽא־שְׁלָחֲךָ֣ יְהוָ֔ה וְאַתָּ֗ה הִבְטַ֛חְתָּ אֶת־הָעָ֥ם הַזֶּ֖ה עַל־שָֽׁקֶר׃
records.gloss: And said Jeremiah the prophet to Hananiah the prophet, Hear please, Hananiah; not has sent you Yahweh, and you have made trust the people the this upon a lie.
pieces: Then the prophet Jeremiah said to the prophet Hananiah, "Hear this, Hananiah! {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has not sent you, and yet you have made this people trust in a lie.

L.15: And Jeremiah the prophet said to Hananiah the prophet, "Hear now, Hananiah: {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has not sent you, and you have made this people trust in a lie.

R.15: Then the prophet Jeremiah said to Hananiah, "Listen, Hananiah! {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} did not send you. You have made these people believe a lie and trust in it.

decisions.choice: a lie: a message the LORD did not give
decisions.reason: Jeremiah uses the word for prophets who speak their own ideas in the LORD's name (14:14; 23:25-32; 27:10, 14-16).

decisions.choice: and you: an emphatic "you", setting what Hananiah did against what the LORD did not do
decisions.reason: The LORD did not send him, yet he made the people trust his word.

decisions.choice: made trust: gave the people a false sense of safety
decisions.reason: The same verb is used for trusting in deceptive words about the temple (7:4, 8).

decisions.choice: and yet
decisions.reason: Balanced brings out the contrast carried by the emphatic "you".

records.source: לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה הִנְנִי֙ מְשַֽׁלֵּֽחֲךָ֔ מֵעַ֖ל פְּנֵ֣י הָאֲדָמָ֑ה הַשָּׁנָה֙ אַתָּ֣ה מֵ֔ת כִּֽי־סָרָ֥ה דִבַּ֖רְתָּ אֶל־יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: Therefore thus says Yahweh, Behold I [am] sending you from upon [the] face of the ground; the year you [will] die, for rebellion you have spoken against Yahweh.
pieces: Therefore {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says this: I am about to send you off the face of the earth. This year you will die, because you have urged rebellion against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."

L.16: Therefore thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: See, I [am] sending you away from upon the face of the ground. This year you [will] die, for you have spoken rebellion against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."

R.16: So this is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: I did not send you, but now I am going to send you away, off the face of the earth. You will die before this year is over, because you have told the people to turn against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."

decisions.choice: sending you away: a play on "send"; the LORD did not send Hananiah as a prophet, but he will send him off in death
decisions.reason: The verb is the same root as "sent" in verse 15. Being sent away from the face of the ground means being removed from the land of the living.

decisions.choice: spoken rebellion against the LORD: the charge of Deuteronomy 13:6
decisions.reason: The law says that a prophet who speaks rebellion against the LORD must die (Deuteronomy 13:6). Hananiah's message turned the people from what the LORD had told them to do (27:12-15). The same charge is made against Shemaiah in 29:32.

decisions.choice: this year you will die: a short, dated prediction that can be tested
decisions.reason: The word against Hananiah gives a time within the year, much shorter than his own two years (verse 3); verse 17 shows it came true.

decisions.choice: I did not send you, but now
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the play on "send" from verse 15, which the Hebrew carries by repeating the verb.

decisions.choice: urged rebellion (Balanced); told the people to turn against (Readable)
decisions.reason: The wording follows Deuteronomy 13:6, which this verse echoes.

records.source: וַיָּ֛מָת חֲנַנְיָ֥ה הַנָּבִ֖יא בַּשָּׁנָ֣ה הַהִ֑יא בַּחֹ֖דֶשׁ הַשְּׁבִיעִֽי׃פ
records.gloss: And died Hananiah the prophet in the year the that, in the month the seventh.
pieces: And the prophet Hananiah died that same year, in the seventh month.

L.17: And Hananiah the prophet died in that year, in the seventh month.

R.17: Hananiah died that same year, in the seventh month.

decisions.choice: the seventh month: two months after the fifth month of verse 1
decisions.reason: The word of verse 16 came true within two months, while Hananiah's "two years" did not. By the test of verse 9, the LORD had sent Jeremiah and not Hananiah.
